current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable with a neck issue.
He is in the projected Jazz starting lineup with Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic.
Utah has Jaren Jackson Jr. for a full season and added rookie Darryn Peterson, so Markkanen shares usage with Jackson, Peterson and Keyonte George.
Experts expect him to produce less than last season on a more balanced offense with lower usage. One projection is 34 minutes and a usage rate of 25.
The Jazz plan to try to win this season, not tank. One projection has them at 43 wins and a 7th or 8th seed.
Experts agree that fears of Utah resting or shutting him down are misplaced, and that the market is marking him down for those fears.
In category leagues a rank around 32 is about right for him. Do not take him in the first round.
Experts see him as underrated at an ADP in the 40s, and as a steal at his ESPN ADP of 77 to 89.
In one expert auction mock he sold for 30 USD. The expert had hoped to get him for 21 to 22 USD.
He is the longest-tenured NBA player who has never played in a playoff game, which adds pressure this season.

durable.text: He is a strong FT% asset. He shoots about 89 to 90% on 5 to 6 attempts per game, which clearly lifts a team's FT%.
He is a scoring forward who makes about 3 threes per game, far above the norm for his position. He also gives good points and rebounds.
He adds little in assists, steals and blocks, and his FG% is a little below average.
He has missed many games in his career. Some were real injuries and some were tank-driven holdouts.

Experts disagree on his health risk. One says he cannot stay healthy whether or not Utah tanks. Others call his past injury concerns mostly exaggerated, or say the missed games were real injuries rather than rest.
For years he has played several short stints per game, coming out early and going back in.
His best position is power forward. He has played out of position at small forward for the last couple of years.

note: He is a forward who brings strong FT% on volume plus threes, points and rebounds. That fits any build that wants FT% and frontcourt threes. Expect a price above the 16 USD he cost in our league last season: Yahoo values him at 29 USD (average cost 20.7) and he went for 30 USD in an expert mock, while ESPN has him at 20 USD (average cost 13.1). A bid in the low to mid 20s matches the experts' rank of about 30 to 32. Early in the season, check the neck issue (Yahoo Q), his shot share next to Jaren Jackson Jr. and Darryn Peterson, and whether he stays healthy after playing only 42 games last season.
